objectives.title: Find details in a short text

lessons.explanation: An infinitive names an action and ends in -ar, -er or -ir. After me gusta, keep the activity in its infinitive. Do not conjugate it for yo in this construction.
commonMistakes: Me gusta estudio is incorrect for I like to study; use estudiar.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Place no before me gusta to negate. A mí también agrees with a positive statement; a mí tampoco agrees with a negative. Use a mí sí or a mí no to disagree.
examples: No me gusta bailar. —A mí tampoco.
commonMistakes: Tampoco agrees with a negative; it is not interchangeable with también.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Read the question first. Find the sentence that gives that detail, and check who, when or where it describes.
examples: ¿Cuándo? Look for the time or day.
commonMistakes: A familiar word alone may not answer the question. Check the whole message.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra strategy lesson; author review, not an independent educator audit.

examples: Listen for names, numbers and places.

stimuli.SpanishText: Me llamo Luis. Me gusta escuchar música y dibujar. No me gusta correr. Mi amiga Ana dice «A mí tampoco me gusta correr». Ana dice «Me gusta bailar». Yo digo «A mí también». En casa me gusta leer un libro. En la escuela me gusta estudiar español. No me gusta trabajar los domingos. Mi actividad favorita es dibujar una casa con muchos colores.
stimuli.provenance: Original fictional passage, authored for Palabra. Not a textbook reading.
